headings.title: Introduction to the Operating Theatre Team
headings.content: The operating theatre environment requires seamless collaboration among diverse healthcare professionals to ensure patient safety and successful surgical outcomes. Team members operate within strict sterile and non-sterile zones, adhering to established roles that minimize infection risks and procedural errors. Clear communication and mutual respect dictate the workflow from the preoperative briefing through to post-surgical handover.

headings.title: The Surgeon and Surgical Assistants
headings.content: The surgeon bears ultimate legal and medical responsibility for the performance of the surgical procedure and the overall care of the operative patient. Surgical assistants, who may be resident doctors, medical officers, or other qualified clinicians, actively help by retracting tissues, securing hemostasis, and suturing wounds under the surgeon's direction.

headings.title: Anaesthesia Personnel
headings.content:
The anaesthesia team consists of physician anaesthetists and nurse anaesthetists responsible for keeping the patient pain-free, unconscious, and physiologically stable throughout the surgery. 

- **Physician Anaesthetist**: A medical doctor specialized in administering anaesthesia, managing complex pain, and handling critical intraoperative emergencies.
- **Nurse Anaesthetist**: A specialized nursing professional trained to administer anaesthetic agents and monitor patient vitals under medical supervision.

headings.title: The Scrub Nurse
headings.content: Operating within the sterile field, the scrub nurse wears sterile gowns and gloves to handle instruments, sutures, and equipment directly. They maintain an accurate, continuous count of needles, sponges, and instruments with the circulating nurse to prevent retained foreign objects. Anticipating the surgeon's needs forms a core competency for maintaining an efficient surgical pace.

headings.title: The Circulating Nurse
headings.content: Operating as a non-sterile team member, the circulating nurse manages the overall environment of the operating room. Their duties include patient positioning, documenting intraoperative events, managing specimen collection, and opening sterile supplies for the scrub nurse without breaking sterility rules.

headings.title: Support Staff: Health Orderlies and Students
headings.content: Support personnel complete the operating theatre ecosystem by handling essential logistical and educational functions. Health orderlies manage heavy lifting, patient transport, waste disposal, and room turnaround between cases. Nursing students observe and participate under direct supervision to bridge classroom theory with clinical reality.
